The '''2020–21 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team''' represented [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University]] during the [[2020–21 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Hokies were led by second-year head coach [[Mike Young (basketball)|Mike Young]] and played their home games at [[Cassell Coliseum]] in [[Blacksburg, Virginia]], as members of the [[Atlantic Coast Conference]].<ref name=Young>{{cite news|url=http://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/26464970/va-tech-hires-wofford-young-new-coach |title=Va. Tech hires Wofford's Young as new coach |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |website=ESPN.com |date=April 7, 2019 |accessdate=April 8, 2019}}</ref> In a season limited due to the ongoing [[COVID-19 pandemic in the United States|COVID-19 pandemic]], the Hokies finished the season 15–7, 9–4 in [[2020–21 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]], to finish in third place. They lost to [[2020–21 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the quarterfinals of the [[2021 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] after earning a double-bye into the quarterfinals. They received an at-large bid to the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 10 seed in the [[2021 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#South Regional|South Region]] where they lost to [[2020–21 Florida Gators men's basketball team|Florida]] in the first round.

==Previous season==
The [[2019–20 Virginia Tech Hokies men's basketball team|Hokies]] finished the [[2019–20 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2019–20 season]] 16–16, 7–13 in [[2019–20 Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball season|ACC play]] to finish in a tie for 10th place. They lost to [[2019–20 North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball team|North Carolina]] in the first round of the [[2020 ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]]. The tournament was thereafter canceled due to the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic.<ref name="ACC Tournament">{{cite web |title=Statement from ACC on Men's Basketball Tournament |url=https://theacc.com/news/2020/3/12/statement-from-acc-on-mens-basketball-tournament.aspx |website=theacc.com |publisher=Atlantic Coast Conference |accessdate=12 March 2020}}</ref> The [[2020 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] and all other postseason tournaments were also cancelled due to the pandemic.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships|title=NCAA cancels remaining winter and spring championships|last=|first=|date=|website=|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200312202043/http://www.ncaa.org/about/resources/media-center/news/ncaa-cancels-remaining-winter-and-spring-championships |archive-date=2020-03-12 |access-date=}}</ref>
